topics.title: Your first animation
topics.intro: Draw a ball, give it a Position track, key it in two places and play it. That is the whole idea of SVGcinema, in six steps.
topics.goal: A ball rolls across the ground in two seconds, rests for a second at the end of the 3-second animation, and starts over: one track, two keyframes.

steps.title: Pick the Ellipse tool
steps.text: Press <kbd>O</kbd>. The Ellipse tool lives in the shapes button of the tools on the left: hold it to see the other shapes.

steps.title: Draw a ball
steps.text: Drag on the canvas, just above the ground. Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> to keep it round. The new ball is selected, and the inspector on the right shows everything you can set on it.
steps.do: Drag on the canvas, above the ground. <kbd>Shift</kbd> keeps it round.

steps.title: Start a Position track
steps.text: Click {◆} beside Position in the inspector. Position gets its own row on the timeline, with a keyframe at the playhead, and the diamond turns amber.

steps.title: Move the playhead to 2s
steps.text: Drag the red playhead along the time ruler at the top of the timeline, to 2s. The inspector now shows the values at that moment.

steps.title: Move the ball
steps.text: Press <kbd>V</kbd> for the Select tool and drag the ball to the right, or type a bigger X in Position. A second keyframe lands at 2s: the editor fills in everything between the two.
steps.do: <kbd>V</kbd>, then drag the ball to the right.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press <kbd>Space</kbd>. The ball rolls across in two seconds, rests until the end of the animation (3 seconds in a new project), and starts over, as a new project loops forever. Next, give it a better feel in Easing.

topics.note: Every property in the inspector works the same way: start its track with {◆}, then change it at another time. A property without a track just changes, everywhere in time.
keys: Add a position keyframe at the playhead

topics.title: Keyframes and tracks
topics.intro: Every property in the inspector can be animated. Start a track on it with {◆}, then change the value at another time: a keyframe lands under the playhead, and the editor fills in everything between.
topics.goal: The sun turns a quarter in two seconds, rests for a second, and starts over: two keyframes on one track.

steps.title: Select the sun
steps.text: Click the sun on the canvas, or its row in the Layers panel. The inspector shows everything you can set on it.
steps.do: Click the sun, or its row in Layers.

steps.title: Start a track
steps.text: Click {◆} beside Rotate. Rotate gets its own row on the timeline, with a keyframe at the playhead, and the diamond turns amber.

steps.title: Move the playhead
steps.text: Drag the red playhead along the time ruler to 2s. The inspector now shows the values at that moment.

steps.title: Change the value
steps.text: Type 90 in Rotate and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>, or drag its label. A second keyframe appears at 2s, and the sun turns on the canvas.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press <kbd>Space</kbd>. The sun turns until 2s, rests until the end of the 3-second animation, and starts over. To change how it moves between two keys, see Easing.

topics.note: A property without a track just changes, everywhere in time. Once it has a track, every change adds or updates a keyframe at the playhead. To keep a track's keys but stop using them for a while, freeze it with the snowflake beside its name in the timeline.

Easing
topics.intro: Easing is how a property gets from one keyframe to the next: at an even speed, speeding up, slowing down, overshooting or bouncing. Each keyframe has its own, for the way to the next key.
topics.goal: The ball drops and bounces to a stop, then starts over: the same two keyframes, with Bounce out.

steps.title: Play it as it is
steps.text: Press <kbd>Space</kbd>. The ball falls at one even speed and stops dead: its keyframe is set to Linear.
steps.do: Press <kbd>Space</kbd> and watch the ball fall.

steps.title: Pick the way between the keys
steps.text: In the timeline, click the line between the ball's two keyframes. That selects the first key: its easing is the way to the next one.
steps.do: Click the line between the two keyframes.

steps.title: Open the Easing panel
steps.text: Click the curve button in the timeline's header, left of Animate. The Easing panel opens above the timeline.

steps.title: Pick Out, then Bounce
steps.text: Click Out at the top of the panel, then Bounce. The curve shows the new timing: the ball now lands and bounces.

steps.title: Play it again
steps.text: Press <kbd>Space</kbd>. Same two keys, a different feel. Drag the curve's two handles for a timing of your own, and save it as a preset.

topics.note: In, Out and In-Out decide where the change happens: In starts slowly, Out ends slowly, In-Out does both. Hold keeps the value until the next key, then jumps.
